top_stories.title: Bitcoin Falls to Multi-Month Low Amid Rate Hike Fears and ETF Outflows
points: Bitcoin dropped sharply, with prices cited between $67,555 and $68,935 depending on timing, marking its lowest level since August (roughly a 12-week low).
The decline erased about 21% from Bitcoin's autumn peak near $86,000.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that let investors buy Bitcoin exposure through traditional stock markets) saw six consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.49 billion, signaling weakening institutional demand.
A wave of leveraged long position liquidations (forced sales of borrowed-money bets that price would rise) triggered the immediate sell-off.
Hot inflation data has cemented market expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December, reducing the appeal of non-yielding assets like Bitcoin.

unique_angles.point: Decrypt's prediction market assigns an 81% probability Bitcoin falls to $67,500 by month-end, with 16% odds of reaching $60,000 (near June's $59,000 low).
Two key upcoming dates could determine direction: Fed meeting minutes on November 18 and fresh Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data on November 25.

Analysts cite deeper demand weakness across ETFs, stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to stable assets like the US dollar), and corporate treasuries occurring simultaneously, not just the liquidation spike.

Nvidia's leadership transition (Jensen Huang stepping down, Colette Kress promoted from CFO to CEO) and Congressional scrutiny of chip exports to China have added to broader market risk-off sentiment.

items.title: Texas Bitcoin Legislation
points: A Texas bill would permit every city and county in the state to independently purchase up to $10 million in bitcoin.
If passed, this could represent substantial institutional adoption across hundreds of municipal governments.

items.title: Strategy Removed From Stock Indexes Despite Profits
points: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) reported $19.5 billion in profit, yet MSCI is removing it from its stock indexes.

items.title: UK Crypto Laundering Risk Ahead of FATF Review
points: Crypto-related money laundering is considered a 'material risk' for the UK ahead of a review by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the global body that sets anti-money-laundering standards.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs posted six consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.49 billion, driven by persistent inflation data cementing December rate hike odds
A wave of leveraged long position liquidations triggered the immediate sell-off, but analysts cite deeper demand weakness across ETFs, stablecoins, and corporate treasuries simultaneously
Nvidia's leadership transition to Colette Kress and Congressional scrutiny of chip exports to China have added to broader market risk-off sentiment

sections.title: Bitcoin's Multi-Factor Collapse
points: Price fell from $86,000 peak to $68,935, a 21% decline driven by three converging pressures: leveraged liquidations, ETF redemptions ($1.49 billion over six days), and Fed rate hike fears
Hot inflation data published Friday cemented market expectations of a December interest-rate increase, reducing appeal of non-yielding assets like Bitcoin
Spot ETF outflows signal institutional demand weakness, compounded by declining stablecoin liquidity and corporate treasury selling pressure all occurring simultaneously

sections.title: Fed Policy and Macro Headwinds Ahead
points: Two key dates will likely determine near-term direction: Fed meeting minutes on November 18 and fresh Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data on November 25
Market participants overwhelmingly expect a rate hike in December, which tightens financial conditions and typically pressures risk assets
Nvidia's unexpected CEO transition (Jensen Huang stepping down, Colette Kress promoted from finance chief) has further deteriorated risk appetite in tech-heavy portfolios

sections.title: Market Expectations for Further Downside
points: Decrypt's prediction market assigns 81% probability to Bitcoin reaching $67,500 by November 30 and roughly 50% odds of $65,000
A $60,000 test (near the June low of $59,000) carries 16% odds according to derivatives traders
The 12-week low suggests momentum has shifted decisively, with technical support levels now under test
